title: Refinement compatibility of strict-local module restrictions
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $f:X\to Y$ a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ a geometric point with algebraically closed $\Omega$ [def-weil-geometric-point], and $F$ a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Put $Z=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O^{sh}_{Y,s})$ and $p:Z\to X$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit; def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. Let $J$ be the small model of ring-written affine pointed neighbourhoods of $s$, and $B:J\to X_{et}$ their base-change diagram. For $j\in J$, let $\delta_j:Z\to p^{-1}B_j$ be the graph of the strict-henselization limit leg after the pullback symmetry. Define $r_j:F(B_j)\to\Gamma(Z,p^{-1}F)$ as the adjunction unit at $B_j$, restriction along $\delta_j$, and the inverse terminal-section/global-section isomorphism. Then for every refinement $a:j\to k$, $F(B(a))\,;r_j=r_k$. This holds without a quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness hypothesis.

proof.text: Use the base-change cone with its two projection formulas. Pullback extensionality identifies its legs with strictHenselizationBaseChangeMap.

Naturality of those cone legs gives baseChangeMap_j followed by B(a) equal to baseChangeMap_k. Compose with pullback symmetry. Two applications of pullback extensionality prove δ_j followed by p.Etale.map B(a) equals δ_k.

Naturality of the module adjunction unit moves F(B(a)) past the unit. Contravariant functoriality and the preceding graph identity identify the two restrictions. Postcompose with the common inverse terminal-section identification.
